raw_case_text: A 60-year-old female presented with a 3-week history of tongue swelling, periorbital edema, and conjunctival injection. Associated symptoms included generalized fatigue, diffuse arthralgias, and a rash. Medical history was significant for well controlled hypertension. Physical examination was significant for tongue edema, right mandibular lymph node enlargement, a petechial rash on legs and buccal mucosa (Figures 1 and 2) and ridged nails (Figure 3). Significant laboratory investigations included: WBC 4.8 K/uL (4.0-11.0), Hb 10.7 gm/dL (12.0-15.0), Hct 33.5% (39.0-43.0), platelets 302 K/uL (125-490), AST 85U/L (<33), ALT 75U/L (<32), ESR 98 mm/h (0-20), CRP 9.0 mg/L (0-5), positive ANA, RF 86 IU/mL (1-3), C3 26 mg/dL (90-180), C4 2 mg/dL (10-40), total complement (CH50) 0 CAE units (60-144). A computed tomography scan of the neck showed multiple bilateral lymph nodes throughout the neck. At this point, her presentation was highly suspicious for an autoimmune process. Additional investigations were ordered; she was empirically started on steroids and discharged with outpatient rheumatology follow-up. The following day she returned complaining of severe epigastric pain and nausea. Electrocardiogram was significant for ST segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF (Figure 4) and troponin 2.04 ng/mL. She was diagnosed as having acute ST segment elevation myocardial infarction. Cardiac catheterization revealed 90% stenosis of the left circumflex, a drug-eluting stent was inserted. Lipids and HbA1c were ordered to further risk stratify her; results were total cholesterol 168 mg/dL (<200), LDL 96 mg/dL (<100), HDL 34 mg/dL (>50), and HbA1C 5.3% (3.6-5.6). By this time the results for the tests that had been ordered during her previous admission were available; the most salient ones were negative anti-CCP, anti-Ds DNA 1:640 (<1:10), SS-A/Ro 52KDa Ab 182(0-40), SS-A/Ro 60 KDa Ab 112 (0-40), SSB/La IgG Ab 107 (0-40), negative serologies for HIV, hepatitis A/B/C, parvovirus and syphilis. Surprisingly CMV IgG Ab was >10.0 U/mL (N < 0.59 U/mL) and CMV IgM Ab was markedly elevated at 233.0 AU/mL (N < 29.9 AU/mL) consistent with SLE and acute CMV infection. Given these findings, we hypothesized acute CMV infection triggered or at least contributed to her myocardial infarction.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 60-year-old female presented with a 3-week history of tongue swelling, periorbital edema, conjunctival injection, generalized fatigue, diffuse arthralgias, and a petechial rash, followed 1 day after discharge by acute severe epigastric pain and nausea.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient initially presented with 3 weeks of progressive tongue edema, periorbital edema, conjunctival injection, fatigue, diffuse arthralgias, and a petechial rash on her legs and buccal mucosa. Discharged on empiric corticosteroids pending autoimmune workup, she returned to the emergency department the next day with severe epigastric pain and nausea and was found to have an acute inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for 3 weeks of tongue swelling, periorbital edema, conjunctival redness, generalized fatigue, diffuse arthralgias, petechial rash, ridged nails, and subsequent acute severe epigastric pain and nausea.

objective.physical_examination: Initial admission: tongue edema, periorbital edema, conjunctival injection, enlarged right mandibular lymph node, petechial rash on the lower extremities and buccal mucosa, and longitudinally ridged nails.
objective.routine_investigations: Initial labs: WBC 4.8 K/uL (ref 4.0-11.0), hemoglobin 10.7 g/dL (ref 12.0-15.0), hematocrit 33.5% (ref 39.0-43.0), platelets 302 K/uL (ref 125-490), AST 85 U/L (ref <33), ALT 75 U/L (ref <32), ESR 98 mm/h (ref 0-20), and CRP 9.0 mg/L (ref 0-5). Autoimmune/complement panel: ANA positive, anti-dsDNA 1:640 (ref <1:10), rheumatoid factor 86 IU/mL (ref 1-3), anti-CCP negative, SS-A/Ro 52 kDa 182 (ref 0-40), SS-A/Ro 60 kDa 112 (ref 0-40), SS-B/La IgG 107 (ref 0-40), severely depressed complement C3 26 mg/dL (ref 90-180), C4 2 mg/dL (ref 10-40), and total complement CH50 0 CAE units (ref 60-144). Viral/infectious serologies: CMV IgG >10.0 U/mL (normal <0.59) and CMV IgM markedly elevated at 233.0 AU/mL (normal <29.9 AU/mL); HIV, hepatitis A/B/C, parvovirus, and syphilis serologies were negative. Readmission cardiac workup: ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF; serum troponin elevated at 2.04 ng/mL; total cholesterol 168 mg/dL, LDL 96 mg/dL, HDL 34 mg/dL, and HbA1c 5.3%.
objective.advanced_workup: Neck CT demonstrated multiple bilateral enlarged cervical lymph nodes. Urgent coronary angiography on readmission revealed a 90% stenosis of the left circumflex coronary artery, which was treated with drug-eluting stent placement.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Diagnosed with newly identified systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) / Sjogren's overlap (confirmed by positive ANA, anti-dsDNA 1:640, anti-SS-A/Ro, anti-SS-B/La, and profound hypocomplementemia with C3 26 mg/dL, C4 2 mg/dL, and CH50 0 CAE units) and concurrent acute cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection (confirmed by markedly elevated CMV IgM of 233.0 AU/mL and CMV IgG >10.0 U/mL), complicated by acute inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (90% left circumflex artery stenosis) managed with primary percutaneous coronary intervention and drug-eluting stent implantation alongside systemic corticosteroids.
